content:
robo-incident-bot: [CRITICAL] Dedicated pool 'northforge-dedicated' GPU saturation detected for tenant NorthForge. Trigger: sustained GPU util >=95% across pool for 4m. P40x nodes reporting memory pressure. p90 latency for text-generation API now ~1.2s. Incident ID INC-20260315-172945

maya: paging oncall (moved to this thread). I have the initial alert. Pulling pool metrics and recent deploys.

sam: I see a spike from that tenant — traffic doubled after an internal job kicked off ~10:21 UTC. Not seeing any recent model updates.

lin: FYI devon (AE) notified NorthForge at 10:24 UTC that we were investigating latency. They confirmed an internally-scheduled batch that they forgot to disable.

maya: quick checks:
```
# pool status
curl -s https://infra-api.internal/pools/northforge-dedicated/metrics | jq '.gpus | {util,mem_used,queued_requests}'
# sample output
{ "util": 98, "mem_used": "92%", "queued_requests": 64 }
```

sam: GPUs are pinned to tenant; autoscale policy is "fixed-reserve" with burst disabled (tenant requested strict isolation). No automatic burst to shared pool.

maya: options on the table:
- enable emergency burst to shared/burst-pool (violates strict isolation SLA)
- manual scale-up: provision 2 additional GPUs into the dedicated pool (est 8-12m to spin up ephemeral nodes)
- throttle/route heavy NorthForge requests to a smaller model variant (lower perf but within tenancy)
- ask customer to cancel internal job (fastest)

devon: NorthForge prefers isolation > everything else. They explicitly disabled burst in contract. If we override, legal/reg implications. I asked them to cancel the job but waiting for a confirm.

ops-rotation: I'm available to do manual scale. If we go that route I'll need infra-eng to approve adding ephemeral nodes to the VPC. Risk: if we add non-reserved capacity we might need to open a temporary exception on billing/commits.

sam: infra note: there is a pre-warmed node in us-west that could be attached in ~9m. It would maintain data isolation (same tenant) but will use spot-preemptible GPU config. Would that be acceptable?

lin: NorthForge just replied: "Canceling internal run now, will take ~3-5m to terminate." They asked for status updates.

maya: temporary mitigation plan: 1) ask NorthForge to cancel job (in progress). 2) in parallel, prepare manual attach of pre-warmed node as fallback. 3) if cancellation fails after 5m, proceed to attach. 4) if attach is not possible, then consider emergency burst to shared pool only as last resort with AE/legal signoff.

devon: Confirmed that if we do emergency burst we must log all cross-tenant access and obtain explicit approval. I'd prefer avoid.

robo-incident-bot: Action log created: INC-20260315-172945 -> mitigation_plan:cancel-or-attach

10:31 UTC - maya: monitoring queue length and tail latency. Current p95=980ms, p99=1.6s. Queue depth slowly decreasing (queued_requests: 58).

10:33 UTC - lin: NorthForge update: "job canceled, looks like tasks are winding down, will confirm when completely stopped."

10:35 UTC - sam: GPU util dropped to 72% on average, mem_used 66%, queued_requests 12. Latency p95 310ms.

maya: good — continue to monitor for 10m. I'll keep this thread open and mark as resolved once stable + customer confirms.

10:42 UTC - devon: NorthForge confirmed cancellation complete and thanked us. They asked for a postmortem and an option to add a secondary autoscale policy that allows paid burst with data controls.

maya: note for follow-up: (1) Customer asks for paid burst option with explicit audit logs and VPC egress controls. (2) Evaluate changing default autoscale for dedicated customers to include a "paid burst" toggle in console, with legal/CS signoff.

ops-rotation: will create a follow-up ticket to infra backlog: INFRA-xxxx (evaluate pre-warm policies & paid-burst UI).

robo-incident-bot: INC-20260315-172945 status -> mitigated (root cause: customer-run internal batch overwhelmed reserved capacity). Time to mitigated: ~11m.

maya: closing notes: no cross-tenant burst used. No data exposed. Customer impact: elevated latency for ~11 minutes; no errors returned. Devon to schedule follow-up with customer for autoscale options and runbook updates.

devon: will coordinate and draft a short post-incident summary for NorthForge and attach suggested config changes.

maya: handing off to ops-rotation for doc + ticket creation, moving to resolved in 30m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:

robo-incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-172945 closed by maya at 10:55 UTC (automated).
